notes.title: Update - Changes to handling player height + small bug fixes
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

First, Root Beer On Tap is part of the Steam Winter sale! Get an additional 20% off of the usual $5.99 USD price! 

Alright, now on to the new updates!

[list]
[*] Calculating player height, and appropriate world scale, is now done at the start screen.  The screen will ask you to T-pose when pressing the trigger while starting the game.  Once you've done this the game world will scale to keep everything in the game at a more comfortable reaching distance than before.  For those of you who had difficulty lifting the mugs onto counters quickly, this should help quite a bit.  If you are around 5'9" (175cm) tall, nothing will change compared to before.  An important note concerning this, there is currently no way to recallibrate world scale.  You'll have to quit and restart the game if you want to change it.
[*] the Grow/Shrink button has been removed from the arcade cabinet, as it is no longer needed.
[*] Added a very short cool-down between quick teleport button releases.  This should reduce the chance of the stick flying back too far and teleporting the player in the wrong direction.  Please let me know if this problem persists, I will look at other options.  You can also change the dead-zone settings in the SteamVR Input bindings. If you find settings that work extremely well for you I'd be curious to see them, so please do post them in the Discussion pages.
[/list]

That's all for now.  If you have any feedback on how player scaling works now let me know in the discussion pages! 

Hypernoodle Games

notes.title: Permanent Price Reduction - Root Beer On Tap is now $5.99!
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

I'll get right to it.  The original price of Root Beer On Tap was high when compared to the amount of content present in the game.  Therefore, the game's price has been permanently reduced by 50 percent, making it just $5.99 USD!  I believe this new price more accurately reflects the scope and content of the game, throughout both Early Access and full release.  

IMPORTANT - To those who bought the game at a higher price.  First off, thank you so much for picking up the game and trying it out.  I sincerely appreciate your support, and really can't thank you enough.  As a token of my gratitude to you supporters of the game, I'd like to make you a promise.  You will receive every future game developed by Hypernoodle Games for free, via a key sent to you via email.  All I need from you who already purchased the game is two things.  First, I need you to send me an email at jon@hypernoodlegames.com.  I will keep your email address on record for the sole purpose of sending you keys to games in the future.  Your email address will never be used for any other purpose.  

Second, I need you to prove your purchase of the game prior to Dec. 16th, 2019.  The best way to do this is to open Steam, go to Steam Support under the Help menu in the top bar, find Root Beer On Tap, and take a screenshot of the purchase date.  Please include this screenshot in your email.  You can crop it as is shown below.  Mine says "Added to your Steam Library", but yours will list a purchase date. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34558781/c9a95cfb213fba59d499345c8fe8109d3900e543.png[/img]

Thank you for understanding, and thank you so much for picking up the game in it's early days of Early Access.  

Alright, in addition to that announcement, Root Beer On Tap has been updated with the following changes:

[list]
[*] Created new input binding files for any controller that has a thumbstick.  this increases the deadzone for teleporting and should make it easier to crawl-teleport forward into a level without accidentally popping left or right instead.
[*] Fixed crawl teleport placing the player in a possibly incorrect position after recentering or when using the "grow" mode.  
[*] Pressing the "grow" button now requires holding the button for a third of a second.  This will hopefully prevent the button accidentally being pressed while the main menu loads. The button has also been changed to a physical one like the rest of the arcade cabinet, instead of a faked-physics button like the pause menu.  
[*] A prompt to always use wrist straps has been added to the first screens of the game. Safety first!
[/list]

That's all for now.  As always keep the feedback coming, it is always appreciated!  

Thanks!

notes.title: Update - Support for lefties and those who find the counters to be far too high
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

Root Beer On Tap has been updated! here's what's changed:

[list]
[*] Support for lefties! You will be prompted to select your throwing hand from the main menu arcade screen when starting the game.  Choosing left-handed will cause all root beer barrels to spawn to the player's right, leaving more space to throw with your left hand.  Lefties let me know how this goes, I'm curious how it'll feel playing the game with the root beer barrels on the same side of the player as the customers.
[*] An options menu has been added to the main menu. Here you can change your throwing hand setting, as well as change the level of throw assist.  "Full" is the default and will be the best experience for everyone, other options are there for amusement but are not recommended.  
[*] Grow/shrink button on the main menu arcade cabinet.  Those who are having significant trouble reaching the top of the counters or main menu controls can hit the grow button, which will increase the scale of the player throughout the game.  I'm looking for feedback on whether or not the current player scale is too drastic for its purpose, so feedback on this is very appreciated.  
[*] Various small lighting changes.
[/list]

That's it for this week! Thanks for taking a look!

notes.title: Small Update - Changes to mug throwing + bug fixes
notes.content:
Hi everyone! 

Root Beer On Tap has been updated! Here's what has changed:

[list]
[*] Mug "Auto Aim" - Throwing mugs should be much easier now, as mugs will fly straight forward down the counter when you release them within a very wide angle tolerance. In the future I am open to adding an option to disable this for a truly "hard mode" but for the time being this update is the new default and only option for mug behavior.  Those who have tried the Early Access Release version of the game, I'm very curious to hear your thoughts on this change!
[*]Taps now fill mugs slightly faster.
[*] Bug fixes to grabbing tips.  When you grab a tip to start a "Can Can" dance, a higher percentage of customers will stop and cheer than before.
[*] Bug fixes to crawl-teleporting. Crawl teleporting to a station instead of using the normal quick teleport is now much more accurate.
[*] minor performance updates.
[/list]

Please let me know what you think of these changes, and have a wonderful day!

Sojimne
Hypernoodle Games

notes.title: Beta Update - Customer reactions, thicker root beer, and bug fixes
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

An update to the Root Beer On Tap beta has just been pushed! here's what's included:

[list]
[*] Customers will now give a small reaction to being hit by a mug of root beer. This is a result of feedback on the latest trailer, where the viewer thought this was a feature that already exists due to the reactions of NPC's catching empty mugs. So it exists now!
[*] the "Lives" UI within each level now has the word "Lives" above or below it, hopefully making it more clear that it is in fact showing the player their remaining lives. Also a new graphic appears when the player is on their last life to make that more clear.  Beta testers, let me know how this reads if you give it a go!
[*] Root beer drains from mugs more slowly when tipped. - Changed per beta tester feedback
[*] A few levels have been tuned for balance, as well as the above change hopefully making levels a little easier now that mugs will on average contain a little more root beer by the time they get to a customer.  Beta testers, let me know how this goes! 
[*] Start screen now asks players to stand in the center of their play space before pressing a button.  This is an initial recentering, so that the player will be set correctly according to that point in their space instead of the default SteamVR chaperone center.  - Changed per beta tester feedback
[*] Changes to NPCs that should improve performance slightly, as well as other performance tweaks.
[*] misc. bug fixes.
[*] Experimental HTC Vive Cosmos support! I've added binding for the Vive Cosmos Controllers, if any beta testers with a Vive Cosmos would mind giving it a try I'd greatly appreciate it, as I don't have the hardware myself. Thank you.
[/list]

Also you may notice that I've pivoted to an Early Access release instead of putting out the full version of the game.  I'll go more in detail about this in an upcoming announcement, but Early Access is going to allow for even more feedback on key aspects of accessibility, and will lead to a phenomenally better game once it's time for full release. Again, stay tuned for more on the subject of Early Access release.

Thanks!
Sojimne
Hypernoodle Games.

notes.title: Beta Update - Windows MR Support, Levels, and more!
notes.content:
Hi there everyone!

It's been a few weeks, but I've got a big update today for all the wonderful beta testers! Including:

[list]
[*] Support for Windows MR controllers! if you have a windows MR system and would like to join the beta, or try the beta out using that system, you now can! Please give the default bindings for Windows MR a try and let me know if there are any errors. 
[*] More levels! I've added a bunch of levels to the game for this update.  Please note that some of these levels won't have background music yet, and some of them may cause some machines to go below frame rate on some machines.  If you experience frame rate issues please let me know in the Hypernoodle Games Discord, and be sure to mention your system specs. Thank you for your help in identifying which levels most need optimizing.
[*] Level progression! You'll now see the name of the level, and how far you are through the game before starting each level.  This isn't quite 100% yet, you'll likely see a flash of the partially-loaded level at this time, just so you all know.
[*] Fixed a bug where NPC's would spill all the root beer out of a mug immediately if the mug wasn't sliding perfectly straight when caught.
[*] The above change made the NPC's drink speed more consistant, but generally just a bit faster. I've gone through and tweaked a few levels but do let me know of any huge changes in difficulty that you notice.
[*] Added buttons to bonus levels, you can now choose to start the bonus level or skip it and go right back to throwing.
[*] various other small fixes
[/list]

That's it for now! As always, let me know of any bugs/crashes you find, and feel free to give any and all general feedback you may have! Please post it all to the [url=https://discord.gg/74SXUDx]Hypernoodle Games Discord[/url]. And if anyone who sees this is willing to Beta test the game, [b]especially anyone using Windows MR[/b], please do let me know over in the discord.  Have a wonderful week everyone! 

Sojimne,
Hypernoodle Games

notes.title: Beta Update - Major changes to difficulty
notes.content:
Hi everyone! 

The Root Beer On Tap beta has been updated with the following changes:

[list]
[*] All counters lowered from 84 cm off the ground to 70 cm, a nice standard table height. - Beta Tester Feedback

[*]Probably more but that should be the meatiest stuff.
[/list]

Please give it a try and tell me what you think.  And what better place to give feedback than the shiny new [url=https://discord.gg/cpgdHY6] Hypernoodle Games Discord![/url]

There you'll find channels for suggestions, bug fixes, general chatting, as well as a place to [b]request a beta key[/b] if you don't yet have one and would like to help me make sure Root Beer On Tap ends up being as good as I can make it.  I look forward to chatting with all of you on Discord!

That's it for now, give the demo a try, break it, and let me know how it goes! Thanks!

Sojimne,
Hypernoodle Games

notes.title: Update to beta release 1.11
notes.content:

[*] Added splash screen at the start which shows the Hypernoodle Games Logo and explains recentering.
[*] Added the ability for the player to recenter themselves in their space, in cases where what is set as the center of the play-space by SteamVR or Oculus is inconvenient for throwing.
[*] Added an extra mug of root beer within arm's reach in the main menu.
[*] Made a small change to how throw velocity is calculated.
[/list]


A note about recentering, and about UI in the current beta:
You'll likely notice that all UI hints, such as the super informative posters, and hints in the tutorial, reflect the controls for the Valve Index Controllers.  The system for determining which controller is being used isn't quite done cooking yet it seems, but in the mean time if you are using an Oculus Rift the button positions are basically the same, minus the trackpad.  Please check the controller binding UI for a detailed breakdown of the controls for each controller.  Note that Windows MR is not yet fully supported.

Also, if you are using Vive wands and are wondering how to recenter yourself, hold the application button down for three seconds.  

I hope you are enjoying the beta, and have a chance to try it out.  I'm still concerned about how throwing feels, so input on that aspect of the game especially from fresh beta testers who have never played it before is greatly appreciated.  Thanks!
